main.claim: Pick one of 15 languages, allow the microphone, and speak. Your words appear as text in that language's script. Copy the text into any app, or open WhatsApp with it ready to send.

sections.heading: How to voice type here
sections.body:
Use the tool in Chrome or Edge on a computer. The words come from your browser's own speech recognition, so there is nothing to install.

1. Open [Voice Typing](https://voice-typing.lazur.app/) in Chrome or Edge.
2. Pick your language from the list.
3. Press the microphone button and select Allow when the browser asks for the microphone.
4. Speak at a normal pace. Your words appear in the box as you say them.

**Speak one sentence, then pause.** The pause gives the recognizer a clear end point, and it is easier to check the text before you go on.

sections.heading: Pick the language you speak
sections.body:
The list has 15 languages: Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Malayalam, Kannada, Punjabi, Urdu, Sinhala, English, Spanish, French and Arabic. Choose the language you are speaking, not the one you want to read. If you switch between languages, change the selection before you speak again.

Each language is written in its own script, so Hindi comes out in Devanagari and Tamil comes out in Tamil script. The text you see is the spelling of the words you said, so a clear voice and a calm pace matter more than any setting.

Chrome and Edge support the most languages. If a language is missing or gives poor text in another browser, open the tool in Chrome or Edge and try again.

sections.heading: Copy, clear or send the text
sections.body:
When the text is right, press Copy. It goes to your clipboard, so you can paste it into an email, a document or a note. Press Clear to empty the box and start a new text.

To send the text to someone, open WhatsApp from the tool. The text is ready in the chat, so you do not need to copy and paste it first. Read it once more before you send, because the recognizer hears sounds and not what you meant. Names, numbers and short words are the most likely to come out wrong.

sections.heading: If no text appears
sections.body:
Check three things in this order.

1. **The browser.** Use Chrome or Edge. If the page is open in another browser, switch and try again.
2. **The microphone.** Allow access for this site when the browser asks. Then check that the right input is selected in your computer's sound settings. Close any call or recording app that might be holding the mic.
3. **The connection.** In Chrome, speech recognition uses an online service by default, so a weak or missing internet connection can stop the text. Wait until the connection is steady, then speak again.

If the box stays empty after all three, reload the page, pick the language again and speak one short sentence. A short test sentence shows quickly whether the mic is working.

sections.heading: Where your words are processed
sections.body:
The page does not do the speech recognition itself. Your browser does, using the speech service it was built with. That is why the browser matters, and why the language list depends on it.

If you dictate every day on a Mac, Lazur does this in any app. Hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

pages.title: Voice Typing Android: Gboard Steps and Browser Tool | Lazur
pages.description: Turn on Gboard voice typing on Android, step by step. Then use a browser tool to speak Indian and other languages and copy the text anywhere.
pages.claim: On Android, tap the microphone key on Gboard, say what you want written, and the text lands in the app you are using. Our tool runs in Chrome and gives you text to copy or send to WhatsApp.

sections.heading: Use Gboard voice typing on your phone
sections.body:
Gboard is Google's keyboard, and its microphone key does the voice typing. Here is the basic way, as Google describes it.

1. Install Gboard from the Play Store if you do not have it.
2. Open an app you can type in, such as Gmail or Keep.
3. Tap the text field.
4. Tap the microphone key at the top of your keyboard.
5. When you see "Speak now," say what you want written.

Say punctuation out loud, such as "period," "comma," "question mark" or "new line." Google notes that these may not work in every language. Some steps need Android 7.0 or later.

sections.heading: Check your language and phone first
sections.body:
Gboard does not support every language. Before you speak in another language, add it in Gboard's language settings and turn on more than one language if you want to switch between them. Then tap the language abbreviation on the voice toolbar to choose it.

On some Pixel phones, Google suggests Advanced voice typing instead of the standard option. If you use the Samsung keyboard, its menus are different from Gboard's, and the steps above do not apply to it. We did not check the Samsung menus, so look at your keyboard's own help for those.

sections.heading: Use the browser tool for copy and send
sections.body:
Gboard types straight into the app you are in. Our tool is a page you open in Chrome. Speak there, check the text, then press Copy and paste it into any app on your phone. It also has a button that opens WhatsApp with your text ready, which saves a step when you want to send a message.

The tool supports the same 15 languages on any computer or phone with Chrome or Edge, including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Malayalam and Kannada. Use it when Gboard does not have the language you need, or when you want a text you can read and fix before it goes anywhere.

sections.heading: When the microphone does nothing
sections.body:
Start with the permission. Open your phone's settings, find the app you are typing in or Gboard, and check that the microphone is allowed. For the browser tool, select Allow when Chrome asks for the microphone, or open the site's permission settings in Chrome and allow the mic there.

Next, close any app that might be using the mic, such as a call app or a voice recorder. Then check your internet connection, because the browser's speech service needs one. Try a short sentence in a quiet room. If the text is still missing, restart the phone and try again.

sections.heading: Turn voice typing on in a few seconds
sections.body:
Once the microphone key shows on your keyboard, voice typing is ready to use. You do not need to sign in to Gboard, and there is no separate app to open for the basic steps.

If you want to test first, open the [voice typing tool](https://voice-typing.lazur.app/android) in Chrome, pick a language, allow the mic and say one sentence. That shows you whether the phone's microphone and connection work before you rely on either.

faq.q: How do I turn on voice typing on Android?
faq.a: Open an app where you can type, tap the text field, then tap the microphone key at the top of Gboard. When you see Speak now, say what you want written. If you do not see the key, check that Gboard is your keyboard and that its voice typing is turned on in its settings.

faq.q: Where do I find voice typing in my settings?
faq.a: For Gboard, the microphone key on the keyboard is the quickest way in, and voice typing is set up in Gboard's language settings. Samsung and other keyboards use different menu names, and we did not check those menus. Use your phone's keyboard help for them.

faq.q: Can I voice type on Android in Hindi or Tamil?
faq.a: Yes, if the language is turned on for your keyboard. Gboard does not support every language, so add it in Gboard first. If you cannot find it there, open the browser tool in Chrome, choose Hindi or Tamil, speak, then copy the text into your app.

pages.title: Voice Typing in Word: Dictate and Paste Text Into Your Doc | Lazur
pages.description: Dictate in Microsoft Word with its Dictate button, or speak in a browser tool and paste the text in. Steps, languages and fixes for when it stops.
pages.claim: Word has its own Dictate button on the Home tab, and it types your speech straight into the document. If you want to speak first and then paste, our tool gives you the text to copy into Word.

sections.heading: Dictate in Word for the web
sections.body:
Microsoft's own voice typing in Word is called Dictate. Here are the steps from Microsoft's help page for Word for the web.

1. Open a new or existing document.
2. Go to **Home > Dictate**. You must be signed in to Microsoft 365 on a device with a microphone.
3. Wait for the Dictate button to turn on and start listening.
4. Speak, and your words appear on the screen.
5. Select Dictate again when you finish.

On a Mac, you can also press Option + F1 to start Dictate. To resume a dictation in Word for the web, press ALT + ` or select the mic icon in the floating dictation menu.

sections.heading: Choose the language and microphone
sections.body:
By default, Dictate uses the language of your document. To change it, select the gear icon and pick a language under Spoken Language. Microsoft lists English (US, UK, Australia, Canada and India), French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Chinese and Spanish as fully supported. Some other languages are in preview, and Microsoft says they may have lower accuracy and less punctuation support.

To change the microphone, open the gear icon in the dictation settings. If you see "We don't have access to your microphone," close other apps or web pages that use the mic, then refresh the page, select Dictate and allow access in the browser.

sections.heading: Say punctuation and new lines
sections.body:
In English, Word understands spoken punctuation. Say "period" or "full stop" for a period, "comma," "question mark," "exclamation mark," "colon" or "semicolon" for those marks. Say "new line" to start a new line, and "open quotes" and "close quotes" for quotation marks. "Open parentheses" and "close parentheses" work the same way.

To see the full list, say "Show more commands" and Word opens a help pane. Keep sentences short when you dictate, so the punctuation lands where you meant it to.

sections.heading: Speak in the browser tool, then paste into Word
sections.body:
Dictate in Word needs a steady internet connection, and it works inside Word only. If you want to speak in another place first, use our [voice typing tool](https://voice-typing.lazur.app/word) in Chrome or Edge. Pick your language, speak, check the text and press Copy.

Then switch to Word, click where you want the text and press Ctrl + V. Our tool does not type into Word for you. It gives you the text to paste, which is useful for drafts in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Malayalam and Kannada, and for any text you want to read once before it goes into a document.

sections.heading: When Word stops taking dictation
sections.body:
The most common cause is the connection. Dictate needs a reliable internet connection, and Microsoft notes that poor connectivity can cause missing or wrong words. Wait for a steady connection, then select Dictate again.

The second cause is the microphone. Check that Word and the browser can use it, that no call app is holding it, and that the right input is selected. The third cause is the account: Dictate needs you to be signed in to Microsoft 365. Sign in, refresh and try a short sentence.

sections.heading: Lazur for dictation on a Mac
sections.body: If you write in Word every day on a Mac, Lazur is built for that. Hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app). Lazur is a Mac app, and a Windows version is coming.

faq.q: Is it possible to voice type in Word?
faq.a: Yes. Word for the web has a Dictate button on the Home tab. Sign in to Microsoft 365, select Dictate, allow the microphone and speak. Your words appear in the document. You can also speak in a separate tool and paste the text into Word.

faq.q: What is the shortcut key for voice typing in Word?
faq.a: On a Mac, Option + F1 starts Dictate in Word. In Word for the web, ALT + ` resumes a dictation after you stop. On Windows, Win + H opens Windows voice typing, which is a separate feature from Word's Dictate button.

faq.q: Why is my voice typing not working in Word?
faq.a: Usually the connection, the microphone or the sign-in. Dictate needs a steady internet connection and a microphone that no other app is using. Check that you are signed in to Microsoft 365, refresh the page and allow the microphone in the browser, then try a short sentence.

sections.heading: How to type Gujarati by voice
sections.body:
Open the [Gujarati voice typing tool](https://voice-typing.lazur.app/gujarati) in Chrome or Edge on your computer. Nothing needs to be installed.

1. Choose Gujarati from the language list.
2. Press the microphone button and select Allow when the browser asks.
3. Speak one sentence at a time, at a normal pace.
4. Check the text in the box, then press Copy or open WhatsApp.

The text appears while you speak, so you can watch the first sentence come out before you go on. If it is wrong, say the sentence again slowly rather than correcting the whole box.

sections.heading: Gujarati is written in its own script
sections.body:
Gujarati is written in the Gujarati script, a sister script to Devanagari but with its own letters and shapes. Choose Gujarati whenever you speak Gujarati, so the recognizer checks your words against the right language.

Gujarati speech often includes English words, especially in work and school. Try a short sentence with one English word and see how it comes out. Fix the word after you copy the text if it is not how you want it written.

sections.heading: Copy the text or send it on WhatsApp
sections.body:
Press Copy when the text is right. It goes to your clipboard, so you can paste it into an email, a Google Doc, a note or a message. Press Clear to empty the box for the next text.

The WhatsApp button opens WhatsApp with your text ready. Pick the chat, read the message once more and send it yourself. Nothing is sent until you do.

sections.heading: When Gujarati text stops appearing
sections.body:
First, make sure you are in Chrome or Edge. Those two browsers support the most languages in the tool, so switch if Gujarati gives nothing in another browser.

Next, allow the microphone for this site and check the input in your computer's sound settings. Close any call app or recorder that may be holding the mic.

Then check the connection. Chrome's speech recognition uses an online service by default, so a weak or missing connection can stop the text. Reload the page, choose Gujarati again and speak one short sentence to test.

sections.heading: Gujarati speech on other devices
sections.body:
Dictation options differ between keyboards and phones, and Gujarati support is not the same on all of them. Check your keyboard's language list before you rely on it. On a computer, the browser tool is a clear way to speak Gujarati and copy the result.

If you switch between Gujarati and English often, pick the language before each sentence. The box shows what the recognizer heard, so you can see straight away when the language is wrong. A short test sentence before a long recording tells you whether the setup is right, and it costs only a few seconds.

faq.q: How to type Gujarati by speaking?
faq.a: Open the tool in Chrome or Edge, choose Gujarati, allow the microphone and press the mic button. Speak one sentence at a time. The text appears in Gujarati script. Check it, then press Copy or open WhatsApp with the text ready.

faq.a: Speak your message in the tool after choosing Gujarati. Then press the WhatsApp button in the tool to open WhatsApp with the text ready. Choose the chat and send the message yourself after you have read it once more.

faq.q: Why is my Gujarati voice typing not working?
faq.a: Switch to Chrome or Edge, allow the microphone for the site and close other apps that use the mic. Chrome's speech recognition needs a steady internet connection by default, so check that too. Reload the page and try one short sentence in Gujarati.

Malayalam has its own script, with rounded letters that look nothing like Tamil or Kannada, even though those languages sit close together in South India. Choose Malayalam whenever you speak Malayalam. The language choice matters, because it tells the recognizer which words are likely.

If you mix English words into your speech, test a sentence first. Watch how the English word comes out in the box, and fix it after you copy the text if it needs a change.

sections.heading: When Malayalam text is not appearing
